correctness.rationale: For every r>=1,n>=2r+1 each edge has a unique short clockwise arc of length 1..r. For k>0, distinct chosen arcs have cyclic separating gaps >=r+1 exactly when the endpoints induce k disjoint edges. An additional edge fits in a gap iff the gap is at least 2r+3, hence maximality iff every gap is <=2r+2. Rooting one of k chosen edges gives (n/k)[x^n]B_r^k and (n/k)[x^n]F_r^k. Contiguous block lengths r+2..3r+2 prove the full support and unique-extremal-block multiplicities, including n=2r+1 and k=1. Independent construction of every edge subset in 19 small (n,r) configurations confirmed both polynomials; this does not prove the infinite result.
residual_risks: Independent finite checks do not replace all-parameter reasoning.

originality.rationale: The complete labeled size polynomials for all induced and inclusion-maximal induced matchings of consecutive cycle powers, especially the min-maximal size and full support, are not obtained from Romeo 2018, which proves only the scalar maximum induced-matching size. Published neighboring results on bounded maximal induced matchings and on other graph families likewise do not provide these cardinality distributions. Best-of-knowledge originality passes, with risk of an unindexed cycle-power or square-line-graph independence polynomial equivalence.
